# omx-clap-core / fuzz_manifest

omx-clap-core's own fuzz target `fuzz_manifest` ([source](source/fuzz_manifest.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-clap-core 0.20.1 (FreeMixer/omx-clap-core at 246923f0).

Splits the input into a plugin URI (a length byte, then that many bytes) and the text of an LV2 bundle's manifest.ttl (the rest, at most 4 MiB), each up to its first NUL, and asks lv2_locate_manifest_names whether the manifest names the URI, checking the answer against the harness's own reading of the rule the header states ("<uri>", or an @prefix or PREFIX namespace and a prefixed name as a whole token). It then asks again with the allocation failing, and asks of manifests the harness writes from the URI itself.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libomx-clap-readers.a of src/preset_file.c and src/lv2_locate.c of omx-clap-core 0.20.1 at commit 246923f0, and fuzz/alloc.c, compiled with each build's flags, as omx-clap-core's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- As in omx-clap-core's own fuzz build, the readers are compiled with fuzz/alloc.h forced on them, so their malloc, calloc, realloc, strdup and free go to fuzz/alloc.c, which counts the bytes the reader holds and can make one chosen allocation fail; the harness's own allocations use the C library directly.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The manifest and URI followed after their NUL by a name character or by NULs get the same answer: the reader reads nothing past either string ([lines 176-189](source/fuzz_manifest.c#L176-L189)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The reader holds at most the URI's length plus 3 bytes ([lines 191-197](source/fuzz_manifest.c#L191-L197)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The reader says the manifest names the URI exactly when the harness's own reading of the stated rule does, including the limit of 16 namespace declarations read ([lines 199-215](source/fuzz_manifest.c#L199-L215)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Whatever the answer, the reader gives back every byte it allocated, also when asked with its allocation failing ([lines 217-234](source/fuzz_manifest.c#L217-L234)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The empty text names nothing; a manifest written from the URI as "<uri>", and at each split into a namespace and a plain local name as an @prefix, a SPARQL PREFIX or an empty-prefix declaration with its prefixed name, names it; the same spellings with one more name character answer as the rule says ([lines 236-291](source/fuzz_manifest.c#L236-L291)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
